newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 23.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 23.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
WASHINGTON - New York ad agency Young and Rubicam Inc. has
been awarded a $440.3 million U.S. Army contract to provide
recruitment advertising over the next five years. *********
LONDON - Advertising and marketing group WPP Group Plc
says it has acquired another 1.8 million shares in media
company CIA Group Plc. WPP has now raised its interest
in CIA to 7.8 million shares representing 12.8 percent of its
issued share capital.
CHICAGO - Foote, Cone & Belding, a unit of True North
Communications Inc, says it has acquired majority-equity
ownership in Venezuelan ad agency, AJL Publicidad C.A.
New York - Fortune magazine has appointed Fallon McElligott
to handle its advertising. The Minneapolis-based agency will
develop print, outdoor and television spots to run in the second
half of the year.
LONDON - The Lowe Group's advertising network, Lowe and
Partners Worldwide, says it has established operations in
Colombia by
taking a minority stake in an agency in Bogota.
NEW YORK - General Motors Corp is teaming up with Sony Corp
to advertise its cars at a suburban Detroit cinema -- not on the
Big Screen, but in the car park outside and with displays
throughout the theatre, the New York Times says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
AMSTERDAM - Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier says
it is to acquire Walt Disney business publishing unit Chilton
Business Group for $447 million.
PARIS - Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says his
group will sell its stake in media group Havas once the stock is
correctly valued on the bourse.
NEW YORK - The sports cable TV joint venture of Liberty
Media Corp.and News Corp.'s Fox Sports is in talks to buy a
major stake in Cablevision Systems Corp.'s Rainbow cable unit
for about $850 million, an industry source
says.
TOKYO - Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd and 15 other Japanese
and foreign companies say that they will form a company in
mid-July to offer connection services for Internet service
providers in Japan.
SYDNEY - The pact between Australia's key media players --
Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, Rupert Murdoch's
News Corp Ltd and its cable TV partner Telstra Corp Ltd -- to
rationalise the loss-making pay television industry will be good
for all players and investors in the pay-TV sector, analysts
say.
PARIS - France's new culture and communication minister
Catherine Trautmann says she will present a draft law to reform
the broadcasting sector in autumn.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
NEW YORK - To pay for the staggering $368.5 billion cost of a
sweeping settlement reached last week, the tobacco industry will
be
forced to put up retail prices industry analysts say.
GUADALAJARA, Mexico - Sony Corp's subsidiary in Mexico
expects domestic sales to grow 60 percent this year to $208
million against $130 million in 1996, the company says.
HAMILTON, Bermuda - Bermuda's lawmakers have voted
decisively to ban McDonald's restaurants. The House passed a
bill which did not mention McDonald's Corp by name but had the
sole intent of stopping former Premier John Swan from opening
one of the famous fast-food restaurants on the island.
TOKYO - Toyota Motor Corp. says it will build "hybrid"
vehicles powered by gasoline and batteries which will be
introduced before the end of this year.
LONDON - Warner Village Cinemas announce plans to build what
is described as the world's largest multi-screen cinema complex
at the disused Battersea power station.
LONDON - British department stores could see sales up 10
percent in 1996/97 as they benefit from increased expenditure on
household goods and investment in improving stores, a report
published by Corporate Intelligence on Retailing says.
PARIS - The launch of a variant of Pernod Ricard's Orangina
fizzy drink, a red-coloured blood orange Orangina, has slightly
boosted the brand's share in a shrinking market, Orangina
chairman Jacques Pfister says.
ADELAIDE - International marketing of Australian wines will
be boosted by the imposition of a levy on exports, the
Winemakers' Federation of Australiasays. The levy will also help
to develop new markets including Asia.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
CHICAGO - Frustrated by traditional marketing efforts to
reach today's teen-agers, a handful of companies are selecting
street wise kids to promote their products for them. Footwear
maker Converse has hired a team of 10 urban youths to distribute
stickers and wear advance versions of the latest shoes.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong is experiencing explosive growth in
trendy bars packed not just with ex-pats but also a new
generation of up and coming young, local Chinese professionals.
"Young Chinese people have spending power. Here people live at
home and they have a huge disposable income," says one observer.
PARIS - Few French people would want to do without a freezer
in the kitchen, but nearly half would be happy to live without a
dishwasher, according to a poll by IPSOS for monthly magazine
Cuisines et Vins de France.
SHANGHAI - The thousands of karaoke hangouts which two years
ago dominated Shanghai nightlife, have shrunk in number and the
crooners of old are now often found spending their cash in
bowling alleys, bars and coffee houses instead says an official
at Shanghai's cable music television station.
